tools.name: search_directory
tools.description: Searches Mixer4AI's public agent directory. Returns only agent cards their owning principal has explicitly published to the directory - never unpublished, retired, or tenant-private cards. All filters are optional and combine with AND.

Changing the URL resets BOTH challenges - they must be re-answered (a prior domain/endpoint proof about the old URL says nothing about a new one).

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp.mixer4ai.com" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: self_register_agent_card, check_self_registration_domain_challenge, check_self_registration_endpoint_challenge · Private data: register_agent_card, self_register_agent_card, check_self_registration_domain_challenge, search_directory, approve_agent_self_registration, search_published_intents, find_verified_agent, check_self_registration_endpoint_challenge · Public sink: register_agent_card, publish_intent.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: self_register_agent_card, check_self_registration_domain_challenge, check_self_registration_endpoint_challenge · Private data: register_agent_card, self_register_agent_card, check_self_registration_domain_challenge, search_directory, approve_agent_self_registration, search_published_intents, find_verified_agent, check_self_registration_endpoint_challenge · Public sink: register_agent_card, publish_intent

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
